title: Areas of regions
competency: Find areas under rate graphs and approximate areas with Riemann sums.

keywords.def: A function whose output is a rate, like km per hour or birr per item.
An approximation ∑ f(xᵢ)Δx of the area under a curve using rectangles.

en.text: For a rate function such as velocity or marginal cost, the area under its graph is the total amount: distance, total cost or total profit. Its units are input units × output units. For constant and straight-line rates, rectangles, triangles and trapezoids give the exact area.

am.text: ለለውጥ መጠን ፋንክሽን (ፍጥነት፣ የህዳግ ወጪ) ከግራፉ ስር ያለው ስፋት ጠቅላላ መጠኑ ነው፤ ርቀት፣ ጠቅላላ ወጪ።

screens.title: Speed and distance
screens.ask: A car goes 50 mi/h for 2 hours. On a speed–time graph, the distance is
opts: the area of the rectangle under the line
screens.after:
On a speed–time graph, speed is the height and time is the width.
The region under the line is a rectangle 2 h wide and 50 mi/h high.
Area = 2 × 50 = 100, and its unit is h × mi/h = miles.
So the area is the distance: 100 miles.
screens.best: the area of the rectangle under the line

screens.title: Areas of regions
paras: Here every function is non-negative: f(x) ≥ 0.
The area under a rate graph is the total change.
Units of the area = input units × output units.

screens.title: Which shape is under the rate graph?
items: Constant rate. Area = width × height. 50 mi/h for 2 h → 100 miles.
A straight-line rate starting at 0. Area = (1/2) × base × height.
A straight-line rate not starting at 0. Area = (1/2) × (sum of parallel sides) × width.
A rate that jumps (40, 30, 25 birr). Add one rectangle per step.

screens.title: v(x) = 3x on a grid
screens.ask: Tap the points. The region under the line from x = 3 to x = 5 is a trapezoid.

points.info: v(3) = 9 mi/h: the left parallel side.
v(5) = 15 mi/h: the right parallel side.

screens.title: Key words
defs: A function whose output is a rate, like km per hour or birr per item.

screens.ask: Area under a constant rate: skateboards cost 40 birr each for the first 50. The total cost of 50 is ___ birr
screens.why:
The rate (birr per board) is constant: a horizontal line at 40.
The region under it is a rectangle.
Width 50 boards, height 40 birr per board.
Area = 50 × 40 = 2000 birr.

screens.ask: Area under a straight-line rate: v(x) = 3x mi/h. The distance in the first 3 hours is ___ miles
screens.why:
From x = 0 to x = 3 the region is a triangle.
Base 3 h. Height v(3) = 3 × 3 = 9 mi/h.
Area = (1/2)(3)(9) = 13.5.
Distance = 13.5 miles.

screens.ask: Area as a trapezoid: v(x) = 3x mi/h. The distance from hour 3 to hour 5 is ___ miles
screens.why:
The region from x = 3 to x = 5 is a trapezoid.
Parallel sides: v(3) = 9 and v(5) = 15. Width: 5 − 3 = 2.
Area = (1/2)(9 + 15)(2) = 24.
Distance = 24 miles.
Check: first 5 h (37.5) − first 3 h (13.5) = 24. ✓

screens.ask: Total profit from a marginal profit line: P′(x) = 0.15x thousand $ per month. Profit in the first 12 months = ___ thousand $
screens.why:
The area under the marginal profit graph is the total profit.
From 0 to 12 the region is a triangle.
Height P′(12) = 0.15 × 12 = 1.8.
Area = (1/2)(12)(1.8) = 10.8 thousand $.

screens.ask: Area made of rectangles: 40 birr each up to 50 boards, 30 birr for 51–125, 25 birr for 126–150. The total for 150 boards is ___ birr
screens.why:
The rate graph is three steps, so the area is three rectangles.
Boards 1–50: 50 × 40 = 2000.
Boards 51–125: 75 × 30 = 2250.
Boards 126–150: 25 × 25 = 625.
Total = 2000 + 2250 + 625 = 4875 birr.

screens.ask: Area as a trapezoid: v(t) = t/2 ft/min. The distance from t = 60 to t = 120 min is ___ ft
screens.why:
Parallel sides: v(60) = 30 and v(120) = 60 ft/min.
Width: 120 − 60 = 60 min.
Area = (1/2)(30 + 60)(60) = 45 × 60.
Distance = 2700 ft.

en.text: To find the area under a curve, split [a, b] into n equal strips of width Δx = (b − a)/n. Use the height at each left endpoint, multiply by Δx and add: ∑ f(xᵢ)Δx. More, thinner rectangles give a better approximation. For an increasing function the left-endpoint sum is too small.

am.text: ከኩርባ ስር ያለውን ስፋት ለማግኘት [a, b] ን n እኩል ክፍሎች Δx = (b − a)/n አድርገን ∑ f(xᵢ)Δx እንደምራለን። ብዙ ቀጭን አራት ማዕዘኖች የተሻለ ግምት ይሰጣሉ።

screens.title: Rectangles under a line
screens.ask: Under y = 2x on [0, 6], rectangles of width 1 using left heights give 30, right heights give 42. The true area is
screens.after:
y = 2x is increasing.
Left heights are the lowest in each strip: 30 is too small.
Right heights are the highest: 42 is too big.
The triangle has area (1/2)(6)(12) = 36, between 30 and 42.

screens.title: Lower and upper sums for y = 2x
screens.ask: Area under y = 2x on [0, 6]. Change the number of strips n.
screens.note: Both sums squeeze towards 36 as n grows. The gap between them is 72/n.

screens.title: Riemann sum
paras: Divide [a, b] into n subintervals of width Δx = (b − a)/n.
In this book the height is taken at the left endpoint.

screens.title: More rectangles
screens.ask: f(x) = x² + 1 on [1, 5]. Change n. The exact area is 136/3 ≈ 45.33.
screens.formula: Array.from({length: n}, (_, i) => { const x = 1 + i * 4 / n; return (x * x + 1) * 4 / n; }).reduce((s, v) => s + v, 0)
screens.note: n = 4 gives 34; n = 8 gives 39.5; the sum creeps up to 45.33.

screens.title: Key words
defs: An approximation ∑ f(xᵢ)Δx of the area under a curve using rectangles.

screens.ask: Riemann sum with 4 rectangles: f(x) = x² + 1 on [1, 5], left ends 1, 2, 3, 4. The sum = ___
screens.why:
Δx = (5 − 1)/4 = 1.
Heights: f(1) = 2, f(2) = 5, f(3) = 10, f(4) = 17.
Sum = (2 + 5 + 10 + 17) × 1 = 34.
Check: 34 < 136/3 ≈ 45.3, as expected for left ends of a rising curve.

screens.clue: Add i² + i for each i.

screens.ask: Left Riemann sum: f(x) = 3x² on [0, 5] with 5 equal strips. The sum = ___

screens.text: Left-endpoint Riemann sums: is each sum too small, too big, or exact?
items: Rising: the left end is the lowest point of each strip.
Falling: the left end is the highest point of each strip.
Constant: every rectangle fits the region exactly.
screens.why:
Rising function: left heights are the lowest, so the left sum is too small.
Falling function: left heights are the highest, so it is too big.
Constant function: the rectangles are exact.
screens.clue: Is the function rising or falling? Compare the left end with the rest of the strip.

screens.text: True or false? For an increasing function, the left-endpoint sum is larger than the true area.
screens.why:
For an increasing function, the left end of each strip is the lowest point.
So each rectangle lies under the curve.
The left sum is smaller than the area (y = 2x: 30 < 36).
False.

screens.ask: Riemann sum formula: for f(x) = 2x on [0, 6] with n equal strips, the left sum is 36 − 36/n. With n = 12 it is ___
screens.why:
Put n = 12 into 36 − 36/n.
36/12 = 3.
36 − 3 = 33.
As n grows, 36/n → 0 and the sum → 36, the exact area.

items.ask: Distance as a triangle: v(t) = t/2 ft/min. The distance in the first 30 min is ___ ft
items.why:
From 0 to 30 the region is a triangle.
Height v(30) = 15 ft/min.
Area = (1/2)(30)(15) = 225 ft.

items.text: Lower and upper sums: y = 2x on [0, 6] with 6 strips of width 1. Pick the lower and the upper sum.
items.why:
Lower sum (left heights 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10): 30.
Upper sum (right heights 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12): 42.
36 is the exact area, not a sum.

The region is a triangle.
Base 6, height 2(6) = 12.
Area = (1/2)(6)(12) = 36.
It lies between the sums 30 and 42. ✓

items.ask: Distance as a trapezoid: v(x) = 3x mi/h for 3 ≤ x ≤ 5. Distance = ___ miles
items.why:
Parallel sides v(3) = 9 and v(5) = 15, width 2.
Area = (1/2)(9 + 15)(2) = 24 miles.

items.ask: Total profit as a triangle: P′(x) = 0.15x for 0 ≤ x ≤ 12. Profit = ___ thousand dollars
items.why:
Height P′(12) = 1.8, base 12.
Area = (1/2)(12)(1.8) = 10.8 thousand dollars.

items.ask: Riemann sum with 4 strips: f(x) = x² + 1 on [1, 5], left ends. Sum = ___
Riemann sum with 8 strips: f(x) = x² + 1 on [1, 5], left ends. Sum = ___

test.ask: Total from a constant rate: 12 L/min for 5 minutes gives ___ L
test.why:
Area of a rectangle: width 5 min, height 12 L/min.
12 × 5 = 60.
Units: min × L/min = L. Answer 60 L.

test.ask: Distance as a triangle: v(t) = 4t m/s. The distance for 0 ≤ t ≤ 3 is ___ m
Left Riemann sum: f(x) = x on [0, 4], 4 strips. The sum = ___
test.why:
Δx = 1. Left ends 0, 1, 2, 3.
Sum = (0 + 1 + 2 + 3) × 1 = 6.
(The exact area is 8: a left sum of a rising line is too small.)

test.ask: Strip width for a Riemann sum: Δx for [2, 10] with 4 equal strips = ___
Left Riemann sum: f(x) = x² on [0, 3], 3 strips. The sum = ___
test.why:
Δx = 1. Left ends 0, 1, 2.
Heights 0, 1, 4.
Sum = (0 + 1 + 4) × 1 = 5.
Trap: 1 + 4 + 9 = 14 uses right ends.

notes.text: Figure 2.16 (Activity 2.17) is schematic: rectangle widths look unequal. Answers use 6 equal strips of width 1.

screens.why:
Put i = 1, 2, 3, 4 into i².
1, 4, 9, 16.
Sum = 1 + 4 + 9 + 16 = 30.
Trap: 16 is only the last term.
